Out of curiosity how did you hurt your knee? If there is an absence of trauma (e.g. falling directly onto the kneecap or twisting the joint) then most issues can usually be resolved with toolbox of exercises targeting the inner thigh, hips and glutes which usually where most knee issues stem from. For example VMO (vastus medialis oblique...aka inner quad) weakness can lead to knees caving inward while running which stresses the inside of the knee joint and can lead to the patella mistracking off to the outside of the joint...you can test for tracking by sitting on the floor with your leg out infront of you, tense your quads and watch your kneecap, if it goes off to one side rather than straight back then the VMO isn't being recruited properly. For the hips and glutes 'clamshells' (with bands if possible), bridges and peterson step ups are typically issued as introductory exercises, single leg press/leg extensions can build on this.

Not a physio but have been in for running related knee issues, unless your knee is giving way when you go to stand up/descending stairs, it's locking (and popping with pain) or you're getting pain with compression of the joint in high impact movement you can probably fix it with squats and fish oil.
